app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:5 — one-line move of useRuntimeConfig into setup

review_cost.rationale: One small real change (cache eviction) and a round of nits; the structure itself needs no rework.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache checks a 60s TTL on read but never removes expired entries, so every URL ever fetched keeps its full parsed JSON resident for the life of the process; walking all Pokémon/move details can retain 100MB+ despite the nominal TTL.
findings.suggestion: Delete the entry when a read finds it expired, and cap the map (simple LRU or max-size with random/proactive eviction).

findings.issue: mapLimit continues firing upstream fetches in the background after the first item rejects, and the remaining workers' errors are swallowed while partially-filled results are discarded.
findings.suggestion: Check a shared failure flag inside the worker loop (or collect per-item errors and reject with an aggregate) so failures stop the fan-out.

findings.issue: useRuntimeConfig() is invoked lazily inside a computed getter rather than once in setup, relying on the Nuxt context being available during render.
findings.suggestion: Hoist it: const config = useRuntimeConfig() in setup, then use config.public.apiBase inside the computed.

findings.issue: An out-of-range ?page= is clamped for display but the URL keeps the bogus value, and Number.parseInt accepts values like '2abc'.
findings.suggestion: Normalise (router.replace to the clamped page or drop the param) and validate the parsed integer.

findings.issue: Header/footer landmarks are copy-pasted between error.vue and app.vue (with plain <a> vs NuxtLink inconsistency), so future shell changes must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract AppHeader/AppFooter components and reuse them in both roots.

findings.issue: PageSection has no id prop, forcing the Moves section to be hand-rolled in app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:84 instead of reusing the component.
findings.suggestion: Add an optional id prop to PageSection and use it for the moves section.

findings.issue: data.ts mixes pure formatters (englishName, collapse, latestFlavorText) with async data access (speciesNames, allTypes, speciesCards), and allTypes/typeLabels re-fetch all 21 type payloads on every request (masked by the short cache).
findings.suggestion: Split pure helpers into their own module (or shared/utils) and memoise the type-label map per request/process.

findings.issue: TypeRef (a type reference) is reused as the shape of the games list, which misleads readers about what the data means.
findings.suggestion: Define a generic NamedOption { name, label } (or NamedRef) and use it for games.

findings.issue: The index endpoint's cold path performs ~30 upstream fetches (21 types, 9 generations, species list) and rebuilds 1025 entries whenever the 60s cache lapses; no server-side caching of the endpoint itself.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the handler in Nitro's defineCachedEventHandler (or a route rule) with a short maxAge so the cold cost isn't paid per lapse.

findings.issue: The app has no typecheck/lint script (and devDependencies is empty), even though the server layer leans on inline casts against any-typed upstream payloads (e.g. app/server/api/pokemon/[name].get.ts:33).
findings.suggestion: Add a `typecheck` script running vue-tsc/nuxi typecheck and typed interfaces for the PokeAPI payloads used.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic Nuxt 4 codebase: clean app/server/shared split, DTO-typed BFF endpoints, reactive useFetch with URL-driven state, and docs-matching 404 handling. The only substantive concern is the in-memory PokeAPI cache's unbounded retention of expired entries; the rest are nits (duplicated shell markup, lazy composable call, one reused type name). I'd merge after a small cache-eviction change plus a nits round.
